pages.hook: Describing people is useful when you look for a friend in a crowd or introduce your family. Learn to talk about looks and personality, and to stay polite.

facts.label: Ask about appearance
facts.sub: “What does she look like?” asks about her looks.

facts.label: Ask about personality
facts.sub: “What is she like?” asks about her character.

facts.label: Weight and age
facts.sub: Comments about weight or age can sound rude to strangers.

facts.label: A famous character
facts.sub: Anne of Green Gables has red hair and many freckles.

pages.polite: Use friendly words like **tall**, **friendly** and **nice**. Do not comment on a stranger’s weight.

mythfact.s: “What does she look like?” asks about personality.
mythfact.why: It asks about appearance. “What is she like?” asks about personality.

mythfact.s: It is usually impolite to comment on a stranger’s weight.
mythfact.why: Many people feel it is a private topic.

mythfact.s: “Anne of Green Gables” was written by a Canadian author.
mythfact.why: L. M. Montgomery published it in 1908.

mythfact.s: Anne Shirley has red hair.
mythfact.why: Her red hair is a famous part of the character.

mythfact.s: “She looks nice” can only be used for clothes.
mythfact.why: It can describe someone’s appearance or how friendly she seems.

lines: I’m at the exit.
Look for a tall man with short hair and glasses.
I’m wearing a green jacket.
**Looking for my sister, Ana**
She is tall, with long dark hair.
Last seen near the food court. Call 555-0170.

compare.br: In Brazil people often make friendly comments about looks, like hair or style, and use affectionate nicknames.
compare.us: In the USA people also compliment hair or clothes, but they avoid comments about age, weight or skin with strangers.
compare.tip: Compliment what a person chooses, like clothes or style: “I like your jacket!”
compare.ask: Describe a person in your family. Say two words for looks and one for personality.

quiz.q: You want to know how a person looks. You ask…
Your sister has long dark hair. You say…
quiz.why: Use has for hair, and hair is not plural.

quiz.q: To say she is not shy, you say…

Reading quest — My sister Ana and a girl with red hair · part 1
text: My name is Sofia, and I live in **Tampa**. Yesterday I was at a park with my sister, Ana. A man named Cole saw us. He asked, “Who is that woman?” “That’s my sister,” I said. “**Do you know him**?” Ana asked me. “Not yet,” I said, “but he looks nice.”

Cole said, “She’s tall. Is she shy?” “No, she’s very friendly,” I said. “**What does she look like**?” he asked. “She has long, dark hair,” I said. “She’s tall, and she has brown eyes.” Cole smiled. “**That’s him**!” Ana said, when she saw her friend Tom with a big dog.

I love to describe people. It reminds me of a book, “Anne of Green Gables.” L. M. Montgomery, a Canadian writer, wrote it in 1908. Anne is an orphan girl with red hair and a big imagination. She goes to live on a farm in Canada and talks a lot. Everyone remembers her red hair.

Describing people is fun, but be careful. Say nice things like “She’s friendly” or “He’s tall.” Do not talk about weight or age with strangers. And if you do not know a person well, you can say, “**Not sure**.”
In the end Cole met Ana, and they talked for an hour. “**I’m looking for** a friend with a big dog,” he said, and he laughed. “You’ll like her!” I said. It was a good day at the park.
